FIELD GUIDE / 02—08

Calculate an L-shaped room without double counting

Split the plan into non-overlapping rectangles and add their areas.

Vijeron · Updated 9 October 2026

Sketch the split

Draw a line that divides the L shape into two rectangles with no overlap. Label them A and B. Record which lengths were measured and which were obtained by subtraction; flag any dimension that needs a second check.

Add areas, not lengths

Total area = length A × width A + length B × width B. Alternatively, calculate the surrounding rectangle and subtract the missing corner. Both methods should agree when the sketch and measurements are consistent.

Separate area from the order

The total describes the surface, not the final purchase quantity. Layout, cut pieces and breakage can change the order. Keep the allowance as a separate, editable assumption.

Worked example

Section A is 4.0 × 3.0 m = 12 m²; section B is 2.0 × 1.5 m = 3 m². If they do not overlap, the total is 15 m².

Pitfall to avoid

Avoid drawing two rectangles that both include the corner where they meet; that area would be counted twice.
